source.title: DRAGON: Guard LLM Unlearning in Context via Negative Detection and Reasoning
source.authors: Yaxuan Wang; Chris Liu; Quan Liu; Jinglong Pang; Wei Wei; Yujia Bao; Yang Liu

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some table layouts are flattened, but the reported values used here are assignable.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own unlearning and adversarial-robustness results, including evidence that some tested attacks do not substantially recover the targeted information under DRAGON; this qualifies the scope of the recovery claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover DRAGON’s reported WMDP accuracy and MMLU utility, its TOFU attack results, and the WMDP AIM jailbreak comparison. Detector-only accuracy results are not rows because they do not measure model knowledge recovery. Related methods discussed or cited without new results are omitted.
record.test_reason: DRAGON is a new inference-time guard: it detects forget-related prompts and injects CoT refusal instructions without changing weights. The paper attacks it with AIM jailbreak, precision changes, French name mixing and typos (Tables 16–17), which bears on F in this new setting. Table 17 also reports RMU (weight-based, Zephyr-7B) under the AIM jailbreak, which bears on A and E.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors say DRAGON gives effective in-context unlearning with preserved utility and robustness to the tested attacks. They acknowledge it needs controlled access and cannot stop fine-tuning of open-weight models.
record.recipe_differences: DRAGON detects relevant prompts and injects retrieved policy and generated chain-of-thought instructions at inference time; it does not alter the base model’s weights. The paper compares this with weight-updating and prompting baselines.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that model size and base-versus-instruct type affect performance; instruction length affects TOFU results; attack outcomes vary by attack and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: The detector-only accuracy stays at 0.88–1.0 under AIM, language-mix and typo attacks (Table 18), and at 0.95–1.0 on OOD rephrasings (Table 19).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Prompt-detection guards for unlearning keep high detection accuracy under paraphrase and perturbation attacks.

record.problems: The paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the relevant attack results. The precision-change attack is not specified as low-bit quantization. The WMDP AIM result has nonzero ASR and harmfulness, and the reported comparison is against an original model rather than a model that never learned the target knowledge.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant rows omitted. Detector-only accuracy tables were excluded because they measure prompt detection, not recovery of model knowledge.

untested.parts: No relearning or fine-tuning attack. The authors state DRAGON does not prevent fine-tuning open-weight models.
No activation-direction ablation or internal analysis of deletion versus blocking.
The 'precision changes' attack is not specified as low-bit quantization and was run only on DRAGON on TOFU.
Only the AIM jailbreak on RMU. Rephrasing, other languages and in-context information were not tested on any weight-based method.
DRAGON was not tested against fine-tuning, activation edits or quantization of unlearned weights. It was not tested under open-weight access.

missing.what: Per-model WMDP bio/chem/cyber ProbAcc and MMLU for RMU, Filter-Prompting, ICUL+ and DRAGON. Includes RMU Zephyr chem 45.8 and RMU Llama3.1-8B bio 66.8 (not near chance).
RMU's own ASR/harmfulness without attack, needed to tell recovery from never-refusing. The paper does not report it.

record.verdict_notes: DRAGON never modifies weights, so its 'forgetting' is refusal steering of a model that still holds the knowledge. Its robustness results speak only to the guard under prompt attacks. Rows r03–r14 had baseline/after mislabelled as partial for negligible ROUGE-L changes. The only weight-based evidence is RMU under AIM (Table 17). MUSE WHP numbers in Table 13 are reproduced from Shi et al., so they are cited results, not rows.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether gradient ascent, Who’s Harry Potter, RMU, or other weight-based methods resist the full set of attacks named in the claim.
No recovery fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples is tested.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of whether weight-based unlearning deletes knowledge versus blocking access is tested.
The paper mentions a precision-change attack but does not state that it uses low-bit quantization of unlearned weights.
Tests AIM jailbreaks and TOFU language-mix and typo perturbations, not in-context information demonstrations or every language/rephrasing attack in the claim.

Tests DRAGON against the reported AIM, precision-change, language-mix, and typo attacks; does not test resistance to recovery fine-tuning, activation edits, or explicitly identified low-bit quantization.

relation.reason: The paper reports robustness results on F (attacks on its own guard) and RMU comparator rows bearing on A and E.

tranche.reason: A new inference-time guard, attacked with jailbreak, precision, language-mix and typo perturbations, plus an RMU comparator under AIM. T3 fits better than the reader's T5.

source_check.notes: ASR and Harmfulness follow Lu et al. 2024 (Eraser) and are not defined in this text. No system has an unattacked ASR. The Table 16 baselines are DRAGON's own pre-attack scores. Precision levels are unspecified. Zephyr RMU numbers match a public checkpoint, while Llama3.1-8B RMU is the authors' own tuning.

statements.correction: Table 17 (Zephyr-7B, WMDP, AIM): RMU ASR 0.7115 vs Original 0.7635; harmfulness 3.3173 vs 3.5615. No unattacked ASR is reported for any system.
statements.problem: None for this study. Note that the original's 0.7635 is also measured under AIM, and the stated caveats (no unattacked RMU baseline, ASR is not a knowledge measure) are correct.

statements.correction: DRAGON (in-context guard, Llama2-7B-Chat, TOFU 1/5/10%, Table 16): KFR 0.98/0.99/1.00 before, 1.00/0.99/1.00 after AIM and after precision changes. Precision levels are not stated.
statements.problem: It cites r03 and r06 of this study but never describes DRAGON. The cited rows do fit F support. The conditions list no precision-change attack and no TOFU.

statements.correction: DRAGON (Llama2-7B-Chat, TOFU, AIM, Table 16): KFR 0.98/0.99/1.00 -> 1.00/0.99/1.00 for 1/5/10%. Weights stay frozen. Limitations: it relies on controlled access to the model or unlearn store.
statements.problem: It cites r03 but names only four methods ('all four'). DRAGON fits the group (frozen weights plus detector and CoT guard) but is not described.

statements.correction: r21: DRAGON (Zephyr-7B, WMDP, AIM) ASR 0.1692 vs Original 0.7635. Route dependence comes only from the Limitations (design statement, no experiment): API access only, cannot stop fine-tuning of open-weight models.
statements.problem: DRAGON's stated access dependence fits the theme, but the cited r21 is an AIM attack through the designed route. It shows reduced ASR, not a bypass via another access route. DRAGON is not named.

statements.correction: DRAGON (Zephyr-7B, WMDP, AIM, Table 17): ASR 0.1692 and harmfulness 1.6423, vs Original 0.7635/3.5615 and RMU 0.7115/3.3173. There is no retrain reference and no unattacked DRAGON ASR.
statements.problem: The cited rows fit 'reduced, not removed', but DRAGON is not described. The conditions (3B-8B Llama, retrained reference) do not cover it: it is Zephyr-7B with no retrained reference.

statements.correction: Remove r21. Table 17 has only AIM against DRAGON (ASR 0.1692). The access dependence is a Limitations statement, not a tested factor.
statements.problem: It cites r21, but this study varies no attacker knowledge, access level or post-training route. It runs one AIM attack on WMDP at a fixed setting.
